chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Tha'laba, from Badr ibn Khalil al-Azdi, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Two signs will occur before the Qa'im (the Awaited Imam), which have not occurred since Adam (peace be upon him) descended to the earth: the sun will be eclipsed in the middle of the month of Ramadan, and the moon at its end.' A man said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, does not the sun usually eclipse at the end of the month and the moon in the middle?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) replied: 'I know what you are saying, but these are two signs that have not occurred since Adam (peace be upon him) descended.'

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Awaited Imam, specifically Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.)
key_terms.تَنْكَسِفُ: Eclipse (specifically of the sun or moon)
key_terms.هَبَطَ آدَمُ: The descent of Adam to Earth

ai.seo_question: What are the unique celestial signs preceding the reappearance of Imam Mahdi?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (a.s.) identifies a solar eclipse in mid-Ramadan and a lunar eclipse at its end as unprecedented celestial omens preceding the Mahdi's reappearance, distinguishing them from natural astronomical cycles. This specific timing, contrary to typical lunar phases, underscores their miraculous nature as unique signs not witnessed since Adam, reinforcing the eschatological framework in Shia hadith literature regarding the end of times.
